title: Preparation of Horseradish Peroxidase Conjugated to Anti-Human IgG for Immunoassays
author: Angel A Justiz-Vaillant
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bjmxkk7n

steps.title: Activate Horseradish Peroxidase
steps.instruction: Mix horseradish peroxidase with sodium periodate and incubate to activate.

substeps.instruction: Mix 500 µg of horseradish peroxidase (in 50 µl NaCO3, pH 9.6) with freshly made sodium periodate solution (1.71 mg/ml).
Incubate the mixture in the dark for 2 h.

steps.title: Conjugate Peroxidase to Anti-Human IgG
steps.instruction: Combine the activated peroxidase with anti-human IgG and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Mix 500 µg/ml of anti-human IgG with 500 µg of the horseradish peroxidase-sodium periodate mixture.
Incubate for 3 hours at 4°C with gentle agitation.

steps.title: Reduce Conjugate with Sodium Borohydride
steps.instruction: Add NaBH4 to the preparation and incubate to stabilize the conjugate.

substeps.instruction: Add 40 µl of freshly prepared NaBH4 solution (5 mg NaBH4/ml 0.1 mM NaOH) to the preparation.
Incubate for 90 min at 4°C in the dark with gentle agitation.

steps.title: Precipitate Conjugate
steps.instruction: Precipitate the conjugate using saturated ammonium sulphate.

substeps.instruction: Add cold 50% saturated ammonium sulphate solution (pH 7.4) drop by drop in a 1:1 (v/v) ratio.

steps.title: Recover and Purify Conjugate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the mixture and dialyze the resulting pellet.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the mixture for 25 min at 4°C.
Recover the pellet from the bottom of the tube.
Re-suspend the pellet in 200 µl of PBS (pH 7.4).
Dialyze against 1L of PBS for 24 h with 3 buffer changes.

steps.title: Stabilize and Store Conjugate
steps.instruction: Add stabilizers to the dialysate and store at low temperature.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of glycerol to the dialysate.
Add 100 µl of bovine serum albumin (BSA, 20 mg/ml).
Store the peroxidase conjugated to anti-human IgG at -20°C.
